title: Quran Knowledge
description: General User → Pro. Familiar Quranic teachings, broader basics and short everyday applications requiring deeper understanding of passages and narratives. Covers learning, recitation, supplication, hardship, preparation, gratitude and responsible interpretation. All questions are Pro level within the General User audience; specialist interpretive disputes and verse-number memorization are excluded.
levelMethod: Pro describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires deeper understanding, connecting familiar teachings and distinguishing common misconceptions beyond Mid, without specialist study. This is General User Pro, not the separate Ultra bank. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Which combination forms part of righteousness in Quran 2:177?

options.text: Faith, worship, generosity and keeping commitments
Correct outward direction with no concern for conduct
Ancestry and popularity alone
Wealth without responsibility toward others

questions.explanation: The verse brings belief, worship, care for others, promises and patience together in its account of righteousness.

questions.question: What response to Quran recitation does this verse instruct?

options.text: Continuing a competing conversation
Attentive listening and quietness
Judging only the reciter's popularity
Treating attention as unrelated to listening

questions.explanation: The verse directs listeners to pay attention and be quiet. Detailed rulings for particular settings require appropriate guidance.

questions.question: What does Quran 16:98 instruct a person reciting the Quran to seek?

options.text: Freedom from needing any understanding
Praise from everyone listening
Allah's refuge from Satan
A guaranteed prediction of the future

questions.explanation: The verse teaches seeking Allah's protection from Satan in connection with reciting the Quran.

questions.question: What does the supplication Rabbi zidni ilma ask Allah for?

options.text: A guarantee of public approval
Freedom from all responsibilities
Knowledge independent of Allah
An increase in knowledge

questions.explanation: The verse teaches asking one's Lord for increased knowledge, alongside guidance to the Prophet concerning revelation.

questions.question: How does Musa ask to learn in Quran 18:66?

options.text: He asks to follow and be taught right guidance
He declares learning beneath his dignity
He demands praise before accepting instruction
He claims there is nothing more he can learn

questions.explanation: Musa's request shows a respectful willingness to learn from guidance another person has been taught.

questions.question: What does Musa's prayer before his mission include?

options.text: A request that truth no longer need explaining
An uplifted heart, ease in his task and understandable speech
A guarantee that nobody will disagree
A demand to avoid every responsibility

questions.explanation: The prayer asks Allah for help with the task and with communicating so people understand his words.

questions.question: Why does Ibrahim say he wants to see how Allah gives life to the dead?

options.text: Because he declares resurrection impossible
To prove Allah depends on human effort
To reassure his heart while affirming belief
Because he denies Allah's power

questions.explanation: In the exchange, Ibrahim explicitly affirms belief and explains his request as seeking reassurance for his heart.

questions.question: What does Yunus's supplication combine?

options.text: Denial of responsibility and a claim to perfection
Blaming every other person
A claim that Allah cannot hear him
Allah's oneness and perfection with admitting his own wrong

questions.explanation: His supplication affirms Allah's sole right to worship, glorifies Him and acknowledges wrongdoing.

questions.question: How does Ayyub address Allah about his adversity?

options.text: He states his suffering and appeals to Allah's mercy
He claims faith makes suffering impossible
He denies needing Allah
He declares all supplication pointless

questions.explanation: Ayyub's prayer names his distress while recognizing Allah as the most merciful of those who show mercy.

questions.question: What two directions does Yaqub give his sons together?

options.text: Stop searching and rely only on appearances
Search for Yusuf and his brother, and do not lose hope in Allah's mercy
Abandon hope but keep competing for status
Assume nothing useful can still be done

questions.explanation: The verse joins practical searching with hope in Allah's mercy.

questions.question: What does Yusuf's prayer show when he is pressured toward wrongdoing?

options.text: He treats pressure as making every act right
He declares himself independent of Allah's help
He seeks Allah's help rather than yield to the pressure
He chooses approval over integrity

questions.explanation: Yusuf prefers prison to the wrongdoing proposed to him and asks Allah to turn the plot away.

questions.question: What practical response does Yusuf advise before the difficult years?

options.text: Consume the whole harvest immediately
Stop working because the future is known
Treat storing any provision as forbidden
Cultivate and preserve grain for later need

questions.explanation: His advice links cultivation, limited consumption and preservation with preparing for the coming hardship.

questions.question: How does Sulayman describe the favor he receives in this verse?

options.text: A favor from his Lord testing his gratitude
Proof that no further responsibility remains
Something that makes him independent of Allah
A reason to despise everyone with less

questions.explanation: Sulayman recognizes Allah's favor and sees a test of gratitude in it.

questions.question: What claim does Qarun make about the wealth he has received?

options.text: He acknowledges that wealth removes no duty
He attributes it to knowledge he possesses
He asks to learn from the advice given
He states that all ownership has ended

questions.explanation: His reply centers his own knowledge and is followed by a reminder of earlier people with greater power and wealth.

questions.question: Which balance appears in the counsel given to Qarun?

options.text: Pursue wealth with no concern for the Hereafter
Abandon every worldly need
Seek the Hereafter through blessings without forgetting one's worldly share
Treat possessions as permission to spread corruption

questions.explanation: The verse joins concern for the Hereafter, a worldly share, doing good and avoiding corruption.

questions.question: What conduct marks the servants of the Most Compassionate in this verse?

options.text: Arrogance and a need to win every quarrel
Silence only when speaking would bring no praise
Judging others solely by appearance
Humility and a peaceful response to foolish provocation

questions.explanation: The verse describes humble conduct and refusing to answer foolish provocation with similar behavior.

questions.question: In the discussion of the Cave companions' number, what response is the Prophet told to give?

options.text: His Lord knows their number best
Popularity decides the correct number
Every proposed number is equally certain
Guessing gives complete knowledge of the unseen

questions.explanation: The verse acknowledges limited human knowledge and warns against arguing beyond a sound basis.

questions.question: What acknowledgment does the companion urge upon entering the garden?

options.text: A claim that wealth lasts independently of Allah
Recognition of Allah's will and that power is through Him
A demand that everyone envy its owner
A denial that blessings involve dependence on Allah

questions.explanation: The companion urges acknowledgment of Allah rather than treating the garden as a basis for self-sufficiency.

questions.question: Which instructions close Surah Ad-Duha?

options.text: Seek praise while dismissing the vulnerable
Treat every request as an insult
Do not oppress the orphan, do not scold the petitioner, and speak of Allah's blessings
Hide every blessing and reject every duty

questions.explanation: The closing verses join treatment of vulnerable people with acknowledging the Lord's blessings.

questions.question: What reassurance is repeated in these verses of Ash-Sharh?

options.text: A believer can never experience hardship
Every problem ends by the next morning
Difficulty makes all effort meaningless
Ease accompanies hardship

questions.explanation: The verses repeat reassurance of ease with hardship. They do not give a personal timetable for every difficulty.

questions.question: Why is it incomplete to reduce righteousness to outward form alone?

options.text: The verse also includes belief, obligations and conduct toward others
Outward form is the only matter the verse discusses
Ethical conduct replaces every act of worship
Prayer and generosity can never be joined

questions.explanation: The verse broadens the account of righteousness rather than making either worship or good conduct dispensable.

questions.question: What distinguishes attentive listening from merely having recitation audible nearby?

options.text: Increasing volume while ignoring it
Giving the recitation deliberate attention
Measuring attention only by audio length
Judging the recitation by background music

questions.explanation: The instruction concerns listening and quietness, not simply the presence of sound.

questions.question: What attitude fits seeking Allah's refuge when reciting?

options.text: Assuming recitation makes dependence unnecessary
Treating the request as a claim to know everything
Recognizing one's need for Allah's protection
Seeking the audience's approval as protection

questions.explanation: The verse directs the reciter to Allah for refuge, expressing dependence rather than self-sufficiency.

questions.question: What learning attitude fits the request for increased knowledge?

options.text: Assuming previous study ends every need to learn
Treating questions as proof that learning is worthless
Using a good memory as proof of infallibility
Remaining open to learning rather than claiming complete knowledge

questions.explanation: Asking Allah for more knowledge reflects a continuing need to learn, not a claim of having mastered everything.

questions.question: What does Musa's request suggest about being respected and learning?

options.text: A respected person can still seek instruction humbly
Respect means never learning from another person
Asking permission to learn always shows failure
Only beginners can benefit from guidance

questions.explanation: The narrative presents Musa asking respectfully to learn. Status does not make a willing approach to learning beneath someone.

questions.question: Why is understandable speech important in Musa's prayer?

options.text: Impressive sound matters more than meaning
The aim includes people understanding his message
A listener's understanding is irrelevant
Difficult wording always proves better knowledge

questions.explanation: The prayer expressly links ease in speech with people understanding what he says.

questions.question: Why would saying Ibrahim's question proves he denied resurrection misread the verse?

options.text: Every question automatically means denial
The verse contains no response from Ibrahim
It overlooks his explicit affirmation of belief
The passage says Allah cannot restore life

questions.explanation: Understanding the exchange requires keeping Ibrahim's affirmation and his request for reassurance together.

questions.question: Which attitude reflects the meaning of Yunus's supplication?

options.text: Using religious words to deny every personal fault
Claiming the words make wrongdoing acceptable
Treating acknowledgment of error as unnecessary
Turning to Allah with humility and responsibility

questions.explanation: The supplication's meaning includes glorifying Allah and admitting wrong, not merely repeating sounds without regard to that message.

questions.question: Does Ayyub's prayer support the claim that faith forbids mentioning one's pain to Allah?

options.text: No, he names his distress while appealing respectfully to Allah
Yes, he refuses to mention any adversity
Yes, distress makes every prayer unacceptable
No, because he abandons trust in Allah

questions.explanation: The passage presents honest expression of suffering together with recognition of Allah's mercy.

questions.question: How does Yaqub's instruction connect hope with action?

options.text: Hope requires abandoning every useful step
Hope accompanies a practical search
Action proves hope is absent
Searching makes supplication impossible

questions.explanation: The verse does not set hope and practical action against each other; it gives both directions together.

questions.question: What does Yusuf's prayer add to a lesson about resisting pressure?

options.text: Confidence makes help unnecessary
Pressure automatically makes wrongdoing permissible
Resistance can include asking Allah for help, rather than boasting of invulnerability
Only public approval can protect a person

questions.explanation: Yusuf seeks Allah's help against the plot rather than claiming he needs no protection.

questions.question: Why does Yusuf's advice challenge the idea that preparation always shows weak faith?

options.text: He instructs everyone to abandon cultivation
He says stored grain replaces Allah's authority
His plan depends on ignoring the approaching need
The narrative itself includes careful practical preparation

questions.explanation: The passage offers a concrete plan for difficult years. Faith and responsible preparation need not be opposed.

questions.question: Why does a blessing not mean that the recipient has no further responsibilities?

options.text: Sulayman identifies receiving it as a test of gratitude
A blessing makes gratitude unnecessary
Every benefit proves permanent freedom from accountability
Only hardship can ever involve a test

questions.explanation: The verse presents favor as an occasion for gratitude and testing, rather than an end to responsibility.

questions.question: What attitude should a reader avoid when learning from Qarun's reply?

options.text: Learning useful skills
Treating personal knowledge and wealth as grounds for arrogant self-sufficiency
Acknowledging the need for advice
Recognizing that wealth can be lost

questions.explanation: The warning concerns his proud response to counsel, not a blanket condemnation of learning or useful ability.

questions.question: Why is using the Hereafter as a reason to neglect every worldly need incomplete?

options.text: The verse makes worldly luxury the only goal
It forbids every form of useful work
The same counsel also says not to forget one's worldly share
It says good treatment is irrelevant to wealth

questions.explanation: The verse combines concern for the Hereafter with a proper worldly share and doing good. Neither part should erase the other.

questions.question: Does refusing a foolish quarrel necessarily mean agreeing with the provocation?

options.text: Yes, every unanswered insult becomes true
Yes, every disagreement requires a public fight
No, because humility requires insulting more quietly
No, peaceful restraint differs from endorsing a wrong

questions.explanation: The verse praises a peaceful response rather than imitation of foolish provocation. Refusing escalation is not agreement with it.

questions.question: What reading habit fits the warning about disputed details in the Cave story?

options.text: Distinguish soundly grounded knowledge from speculation
Make uncertain details central just because they attract attention
Treat every guess as revelation
Assume argument alone establishes certainty

questions.explanation: The verse directs attention to Allah's knowledge and limits argument. It does not invite confident invention of missing details.

questions.question: Which claim goes beyond the lesson actually stated in the companion's advice?

options.text: A blessing should be recognized as dependent on Allah
Saying the acknowledgment guarantees property can never be lost
Wealth does not justify self-sufficiency
The companion urges mention of Allah's will and power

questions.explanation: The verse teaches acknowledgment of Allah. It does not state an unconditional guarantee that property will never suffer loss.

questions.question: How do Ad-Duha's closing instructions connect gratitude with conduct?

options.text: Speaking of blessings excuses humiliating people in need
Gratitude concerns possessions alone
Acknowledging blessings goes alongside humane treatment of others
Kindness matters only if the recipient praises the giver

questions.explanation: The passage places these instructions together, inviting gratitude that does not disregard vulnerable people.

questions.question: Why should these verses not be used to promise a particular person's problem will end tomorrow?

options.text: They state that every trial lasts exactly one day
They deny the reality of hardship
They make hope depend on a fixed personal schedule
They give reassurance without specifying that deadline

questions.explanation: A promise about an exact deadline adds information the cited verses do not supply.

questions.question: A study circle focuses on religious appearance but dismisses promises and helping people. Which change fits this verse?

options.text: Include the verse's responsibilities toward others alongside worship
Replace every act of worship with discussion
Treat appearance as the only sign of righteousness
Ignore conduct whenever recitation sounds beautiful

questions.explanation: The verse connects faith and worship with generosity, commitments and patience. A learning plan should preserve that breadth.

questions.question: During a dedicated Quran-listening session, people keep holding side conversations. What would better follow the verse?

options.text: Raise the audio so both conversations continue
Pause the conversations and attend to the recitation
Treat listening as unnecessary if the file is playing
Judge the session only by its duration

questions.explanation: In this listening setting, quiet attention directly applies the instruction rather than treating recitation as background sound.

questions.question: You are about to begin reciting the Quran. Which preparation follows this verse?

options.text: Declare that you no longer need Allah's protection
Seek protection through the audience's praise
Seek refuge in Allah from Satan
Assume starting requires predicting the future

questions.explanation: The verse instructs the reciter to seek Allah's refuge from Satan.

questions.question: A learner finishes a Quran course and decides there is nothing more to learn. Which reminder fits this verse?

options.text: A completed course makes every interpretation infallible
Good marks mean questions are no longer useful
Prior study removes the need for careful learning
Keep seeking increased knowledge with humility

questions.explanation: The request for increased knowledge supports continued learning rather than a claim to complete mastery.

questions.question: You have experience but meet someone who can teach you something useful. Which response resembles Musa's request?

options.text: Ask respectfully to learn from their knowledge
Refuse instruction to protect your status
Demand praise before listening
Assume experience means you know everything

questions.explanation: The verse presents respectful willingness to learn. The scenario applies that attitude without equating ordinary learning with prophetic circumstances.

questions.question: Before explaining an important message, which request follows Musa's prayer?

options.text: Ask only to sound more impressive than everyone
Ask Allah for ease and speech people can understand
Seek praise regardless of whether listeners understand
Treat clear explanation as a weakness

questions.explanation: The prayer's concern includes ease in the task and making the message understandable.

questions.question: A discussion claims every sincere question automatically proves disbelief, citing Ibrahim's request. What should be checked?

options.text: Remove his answer from the quotation
Assume the question cancels everything else he says
Read his affirmation of belief and reason for asking in the same verse
Treat the passage as denying resurrection

questions.explanation: Ibrahim explicitly affirms belief and seeks reassurance. His words should not be removed from their immediate exchange.

questions.question: Someone shares Yunus's dua as a way to avoid admitting any personal wrong. What has been missed?

options.text: The passage rejects calling on Allah
The words declare the speaker incapable of error
The prayer is only about gaining public approval
The supplication itself includes acknowledgment of wrongdoing

questions.explanation: Using the supplication responsibly includes attending to its humility and acknowledgment, not reversing its meaning.

questions.question: A distressed friend thinks telling Allah about their pain must show lack of faith. Which example is relevant?

options.text: Ayyub naming his adversity and appealing to Allah's mercy
Qarun claiming credit for his wealth
The garden owner's pride in possessions
An instruction to stop all supplication

questions.explanation: Ayyub's example joins honest expression of distress with reverence and hope in Allah's mercy.

questions.question: A group says hoping in Allah means they must stop a useful, safe search. Which lesson fits Yaqub's instruction?

options.text: Hope makes every practical step forbidden
Continue appropriate searching without abandoning hope
Searching means Allah cannot be trusted
Only complete inactivity demonstrates faith

questions.explanation: Yaqub tells his sons to search and not despair. The story brings action and hope together.

questions.question: Friends pressure someone into wrongdoing and say they should trust their own strength alone. What lesson fits Yusuf's prayer?

options.text: Assume confidence makes wrongdoing harmless
Treat peer approval as the final standard
Seek Allah's help while resisting the pressure
Believe pressure removes all need to choose responsibly

questions.explanation: Yusuf's prayer models seeking Allah's help rather than assuming personal invulnerability.

questions.question: A community can sensibly prepare supplies for a foreseeable shortage. Which lesson does Yusuf's plan support?

options.text: Use everything now to prove trust
Assume preparation gives total control of the future
Reject practical knowledge because the story mentions revelation
Prepare responsibly rather than treating planning as faithlessness

questions.explanation: The modern scenario illustrates responsible preparation. It does not give planners Yusuf's revealed knowledge of future events.

questions.question: After a major success, someone says they now have no need to think about gratitude. What does Sulayman's response remind them?

options.text: Receiving a blessing can itself test gratitude
Success ends every responsibility
Only those who fail need Allah
Every advantage proves permanent spiritual superiority

questions.explanation: Sulayman attributes the favor to his Lord and recognizes a test in how he responds.

questions.question: An achiever uses personal skill as a reason to reject all reminders of dependence on Allah. Which warning is relevant?

options.text: A claim that all learning is forbidden
Qarun's proud attribution of wealth to his own knowledge
A rule that no one may use practical skills
Proof that advice matters only for poor people

questions.explanation: The lesson challenges arrogant self-sufficiency. It does not condemn useful study or deny ordinary human effort.

questions.question: A person says seeking the Hereafter requires abandoning every reasonable worldly responsibility. Which correction fits the verse?

options.text: Make worldly comfort the sole purpose instead
Assume possessions remove the need for good conduct
Pursue the Hereafter while honoring a proper worldly share and doing good
Treat corruption as acceptable if the aim sounds religious

questions.explanation: The counsel combines an eternal aim with one's worldly share, good treatment and rejection of corruption.

questions.question: In a safe discussion, someone tries to provoke you into an exchange of insults. Which response fits this verse?

options.text: Find a harsher insult to protect your image
Invite others to prolong the quarrel
Treat refusing to fight as agreement with every accusation
Respond peacefully rather than join the insults

questions.explanation: The verse describes humility and a peaceful response to foolish provocation. This scenario concerns a safe conversation, not ignoring a threat.

questions.question: A storyteller adds guessed details to the Cave story and presents them as certain Quranic facts. What should change?

options.text: Separate the actual text from guesses and avoid unsupported certainty
Make the details more dramatic so they sound convincing
Assume repetition turns guesses into revelation
Treat audience approval as verification

questions.explanation: The warning about disputed details encourages care with the limits of one's knowledge when presenting Quranic narratives.

questions.question: After hearing the garden companion's advice, someone advertises its words as insurance against every possible loss. Which response fits the verse?

options.text: Agree that property can no longer be damaged
Teach acknowledgment of Allah without inventing an absolute guarantee
Promise that no believer's possessions can ever decline
Treat gratitude as ownership of the unseen

questions.explanation: The verse urges recognition of Allah's will and power. It does not offer the advertised unconditional insurance claim.

questions.question: A campaign speaks enthusiastically of blessings but mocks people seeking help. Which change fits Ad-Duha?

options.text: Use gratitude as a reason to shame petitioners
Treat every request as permission to insult
Keep gratitude together with respectful treatment of those in need
Assume speaking of blessings removes duties toward others

questions.explanation: The surah's closing instructions join acknowledgment of blessings with avoiding oppression and harsh treatment.

questions.question: Someone posts that these verses guarantee every reader's difficulty ends within twenty-four hours. What should be corrected?

options.text: Change the deadline to another invented date
Deny that the verses contain any hope
Claim that continuing hardship proves the reader has no faith
Keep the reassurance and remove the unsupported deadline

questions.explanation: The passage offers repeated reassurance of ease with hardship, without specifying that personal timetable.
